claims.text: Nanoscale coherent Fe2Ti or FeTi precipitates can be formed within an fcc Fe-Co-Ni-Mn high-entropy-alloy matrix.
The Fe-Ti precipitates will increase coercivity to above 100 Oe.
Coherent Fe-Ti precipitates pin domain walls through magneto-elastic strain fields.
The Fe-Ti precipitates and fcc matrix form a hard-magnetic/soft-magnetic exchange-spring interface.
Introducing the precipitates will preserve the high Curie temperature of the fcc matrix.
The initial single-phase fcc Fe-Co-Ni-Mn alloy has a suppressed orbital moment and low magnetic anisotropy.
The initial alloy has coercivity significantly below 100 Oe and ferromagnetic ordering well above room temperature.
Aging between 600 and 800 degrees Celsius can nucleate and grow coherent Fe-Ti precipitates approximately 5–20 nm in size without destroying fcc matrix continuity.
Controlled furnace cooling will preserve precipitate coherency.
The Fe-Ti precipitate phase has higher magnetocrystalline anisotropy than the soft fcc matrix.
Local variations in magnetocrystalline anisotropy and magneto-elastic coupling make the precipitates strong domain-wall pinning centers.
The exchange-spring interface produces a domain-wall depinning energy greater than thermal energy at room temperature.
The proposed mechanism can increase coercivity without significantly reducing saturation magnetization or Curie temperature.
The aged alloy will have a remanence-to-saturation squareness ratio greater than 0.3.
The aged alloy will retain a Curie temperature above 400 K.
A kink in the magnetic hysteresis loop will indicate exchange coupling between the fcc and Fe-Ti phases.
The unaged single-phase fcc Fe-Co-Ni-Mn-Ti alloy has coercivity below 20 Oe because of low anisotropy and the absence of pinning sites.
Precipitates larger than 50 nm or incoherent precipitates have reduced pinning efficiency and may lower coercivity.
Excessive Ti can destabilize the fcc matrix and promote a brittle BCC phase.

contradictions.description: The initial state is identified as Fe-Co-Ni-Mn with no Ti, whereas the baseline is Fe-Co-Ni-Mn-Ti. The intervention specifies only thermal aging and no Ti-addition step, so the source and initial concentration of Ti required to form Fe-Ti precipitates are internally inconsistent or unspecified.

Coherency is defined as a precondition for the hypothesis, but finding incoherent or amorphous precipitates is also presented as falsifying the strain-field mechanism. Such a result would primarily show that the prescribed coherent-precipitate intervention was not achieved, rather than decisively falsifying the mechanism under its stated boundary.
